To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the linear stability analysis of the self-similar stiff fluids in 2 +1 gravity shows that all solutions with n > 1 and n <3 are unstable and that none of them are critical.
the linear stability of the homothetic self similar solutions in 2+1 gravity depends crucially on the parameter n and none of these solutions is stable for any n.
the self-similar stiff fluids with circular symmetry in two plus one gravity are not stable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the gravitational collapse of a self-similar stiff perfect fluid with circular symmetry in (2+1) gravity.
the gravitational collapse of a circularly symmetric self-similar fluid in 2 +1 gravity.
the study of the linear stability of the homothetic stiff fluid solutions with n= 0, 1, and 3 in the case of circular symmetry, in the framework of 2+1 gravity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there exists no critical self-similar solution in 2 +1 gravity, and the only critical solution is the Schwarzschild solution in 3 +1 gravity.
there is no self-similar critical solution in 2 +1 gravity.
there are no critical solutions in 2 +1 gravity with a stiff fluid and circular symmetry, and that the only stable solutions are the Minkowski and the Kasner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the case of a circularly symmetric stiff fluid, the only critical solution is the Schwarzschild black hole.
the stiff fluids in 2 +1 gravity are very unstable and cannot be critical.
, except for the n =1 solution, the n = 2 solution, and a special n = 3 solution, the stiff fluid solutions in the 2 + 2 model are all unstable and hence not physically viable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability of the self-similar solutions in general relativity is not inherited by the 2+1 gravity solutions.
, in the absence of a cosmological constant, the only known stiff fluid solutions in 2+1 gravity that are stable and critical are the static circularly symmetric solutions.
the self-similar solutions are unstable and hence are of little relevance to the dynamics of gravitational collapse in 2 +1 gravity.
